reference_role: Accepted palette, darkness, matte and watercolor sensibility only; core editorial geometry redesigned
brand_scope: Independent review articles and lecture-note publication covering quantum, AI and science; no formal peer-review certification claim

concepts.name: Open journal
concepts.direction: Create a beautifully proportioned abstract OPEN SCHOLARLY JOURNAL spread viewed almost frontally, with two broad pages meeting in a clear central binding/gutter. Prefer two restrained beige contours or shaped strokes with generous burgundy interiors rather than two bright solid pages. A short quiet teal binding/fold accent connects the two sides, subtly suggesting connected ideas and current science without depicting circuitry. No text or rules inside the pages. At just ONE outer page edge, let the crisp beige form continue into a short, softly fading watercolor stroke. The first read must be an open publication for thoughtful reading, and the second read a graceful original editorial symbol.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Create one refined original square app-icon artwork, about 1024 by 1024, full bleed, no mockup, no comparison sheet.
Brand: AI Tech Review Letters, an independent publication of current quantum/AI scholarly reviews, technical review articles, lecture notes, and journal-style explanatory articles. The FIRST impression must be reading, editorial interpretation, and publication; sophisticated contemporary science is secondary. This is a serious editorial and learning publication.
The attached previous icon is a visual reference for its accepted dark matte burgundy, muted beige and subdued patina-teal palette and its restrained watercolor sensibility ONLY. Redesign the core symbol according to the concept below. Do NOT keep the old Q or its old two-node glyph unless the new concept explicitly calls for it.
Color: very dark wine/burgundy near #3F1D2B, warm muted beige near #B39B79 and a tiny subdued patina teal accent near #6F9185. The user rejected bright versions. Keep the whole image dark and matte, generous negative space, avoid large pale filled rectangles or white pages. Paint/ink on paper sensibility, no shine or gold-foil effect. Background texture is barely perceptible.
Style: precise, original editorial icon with broad confident shapes, thoughtful page proportions and one or at most two integrated watercolor brush gestures. A single crisp painted edge may transition into a faint granulated wash. Most of the symbol should remain controlled and recognizable at 32px and as a small favicon. Central composition within a generous safe margin for iOS corner masking. Distinct from a generic clip-art book/document icon through elegant negative space and one intentional painterly detail.
No tiny words, fake text, paragraph squiggles, equations, slogans, extra letters, watermarks, frames or UI. No atom orbits, brain, chip, robot, stars, graduation cap, feather pen, bookshelf, stacks of books, laurels, heraldic seal, shield, badge, checkmark, certification or formal peer-review authority cues. No 3D, shadow, glow, neon, splash field, flowers, parchment scroll or antique leather/gold ornament.

concepts.name: Review margin
concepts.direction: Create a single upright MANUSCRIPT/FOLIO page, expressed by an elegant muted-beige outline with an identifiable folded corner and a large calm interior. Place one confident patina-teal editorial annotation BRACKET along its margin, as a symbol of close reading and interpretation. The bracket is not a tick, not a letter, and not a mathematical formula. Avoid internal fake text or lines. Let one short lower beige page edge soften into one subtle watercolor gesture. The object must read as a reviewed article or an editorial folio, not a generic task-management note, checklist, phone screen, or document-download button.

concepts.name: Journal volume
concepts.direction: Create a single slim ACADEMIC JOURNAL VOLUME as a minimal flat publication symbol: its front cover, one clear binding/spine, and one understated paper-edge offset make it recognizable as a crafted journal issue. Use a dark burgundy cover interior framed by muted beige structure, not a bright solid rectangle. A slender patina-teal spine accent gives contemporary scientific character. No cover title or fake symbols. A tiny section of the upper paper edge may dissolve into a soft low-density beige watercolor wash, one gesture only. Keep it planar and icon-like, not a photorealistic book, vintage leather volume, bookstore logo, library emblem, or product mockup.

concepts.name: Editorial R
concepts.direction: Create a sophisticated ORIGINAL REVIEW monogram R whose construction visibly comes from a bound page/folded folio, not just a generic typeset letter. A vertical binding stem, a turning upper page surface, and a restrained diagonal lower page stroke should form a clear R using strong negative space. Keep the page-fold structure legible as editorial publication and use one tiny patina-teal fold accent, no node network. The tip of the lower diagonal stroke can soften into one concise watercolor wash, transitioning from crisp structure to diffuse pigment. The only letter is this structural R; no other text. It should feel like a contemporary science-review publisher's mark, not a flag, corporate consultancy monogram, or ornate calligraphy.
